subject: Orbis Health — where customer data is processed and evidence request
messages:
From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@orbishealth.com>
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Cc: procure@orbishealth.com
Date: Mon, 05 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Follow-up: where does Orbis data get processed?

Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Before we can move forward with a formal security review, our compliance team needs a concise breakdown of where customer request data and derived artifacts are processed and which third-party subprocessors are involved. Specifically: 

- A list of regions where processing can occur for Redwood-hosted customers (defaults and opt-ins).
- A subprocessor inventory (who touches telemetry, model weights, KV cache, backups).
- Whether any data or model artifacts could cross international borders (e.g., US -> EU or US -> APAC) in normal operation or for failover.
- High-level retention and deletion windows for request logs, model caches, and backups.

Can you send those items, and any evidence artifacts (SOC2 excerpt, data-flow diagram, signed attestation) that we can include in our vendor packet? If you already have a spreadsheet mapping subprocessor -> function -> region, that would be ideal.

We may need this by end of week (Fri 7/9) to keep procurement timelines.

Appreciate it —
Sarah
Sarah Lin
Head of Security & Compliance
Orbis Health
(attachment: orbis_requirements.xlsx)

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@orbishealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 05 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: where does Orbis data get processed?

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for the clear list. I pulled together a concise summary below and attached the artifacts you requested. Marissa (AE) and Karthik (solutions) are looped in to help with the timeline and any technical walkthroughs.

High-level processing locations (hosted API):
- Default routing: requests for US customers are served out of our US clusters (primary: us-east-1, fallbacks us-west-2).
- EU routing: we run EU clusters in eu-west-1 and europe-west3; customers can opt into Exclusive EU routing at signup.
- APAC routing: ap-southeast-1 and asia-northeast-1 for APAC customers and customers who opt in.

Private deployment (VPC / on-prem):
- All inference and storage remain in the customer environment; Redwood control-plane metadata (account/usage) may be recorded in the region you select for the control plane.

Subprocessor inventory (high level):
- Infrastructure: Amazon Web Services (compute, S3), Google Cloud Platform (model replication in select regions), Microsoft Azure (optional dedicated regions).
- Secrets / KMS: HashiCorp Vault (self-hosted for Private) and AWS KMS for hosted; optional customer-managed KMS for Private.
- CDN / networking: Cloudflare (edge routing, optional).
- Observability / metrics: Datadog (aggregated telemetry; request payloads are redacted), Sentry (error traces).
- Email / notifications: SendGrid.

Cross-border behavior:
- For Redwood-hosted API, requests are processed in the region selected for the route; we do not intentionally move raw request payloads between regions for permanent storage. 
- Short-lived model replication (for warm pools/HA) can replicate model weights within the same cloud provider across nearby regions for redundancy; we can provide an attestation that no customer PII is included in weight replication.

Retention & deletion (default hosted plan):
- Transient request cache / KV: typically evicted within 24–72 hours.
- Request logs (metadata, error traces): retained 90 days by default; longer retention available by contract.
- Backups / snapshots of internal state: retained per contract; default is 180 days for customer-facing backups.

Attachments I’ve included:
- SOC2_snapshot_202707.pdf (SOC2 sections relevant to processing and subprocessors)
- subproc_inventory_20270705.csv (row-level mapping: subprocessor, function, region, contact)
- data_flow_diagram_orbis.png (example data journey for a hosted API request)

Next steps:
- If useful, we can provide a signed attestation and a completed spreadsheet mapping for Orbis specifically — Marissa can coordinate an NDA/POC attachment and timeline.
- Happy to schedule a 30–45 minute technical Q&A this week; propose Wed 7/7 or Thu 7/8.

Quick note on evidence: the CSV and diagram are redacted for internal telemetry fields; we can produce a more detailed export under an MSA/NDA if needed.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Lead Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
(attachment: subproc_inventory_20270705.csv)
(attachment: SOC2_snapshot_202707.pdf)

From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@orbishealth.com>
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Cc: procure@orbishealth.com
Date: Tue, 06 Jul 2027 08:17:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: where does Orbis data get processed?

Dylan —

Thanks for the quick response and the artifacts. A few clarifying questions from our security team:

1) Model weights: are any customer-specific fine-tuned weights ever stored outside the region the tenant selects?
2) KV cache: is it ever persisted to object storage (S3/GCS) for cold-starts or only in-memory?
3) Deletion SLA: for hosted customers, if Orbis issues a deletion request for historical request payloads and logs, what is your SLA to remove those items from live and from backups?
4) Cross-border copies: can you confirm whether warm-pool replication or HA replication could result in copies landing in a different legal jurisdiction (e.g., US -> EU) without Orbis opting in?
5) Evidence format: we prefer a signed, single-sheet attestation plus the CSV mapping. Can Redwood provide that by Fri 7/9?

Also — if you have a short checklist we can share with procurement (one page) that calls out the pieces we’ll need for contract review, that would be helpful.

Cheers,
Sarah
(attachment: orbis_sec_questions.pdf)

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@orbishealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 07 Jul 2027 14:08:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: where does Orbis data get processed?

Sarah —

Answers inline and delivery plan below. Short version: yes, we can provide the attestation and a contract-ready mapping by Fri 7/9; see timeline at the end.

1) Model weights:
- Default behavior: Redwood does not create customer-specific model weights unless a customer explicitly requests fine-tuning. If Orbis requests fine-tuning, we store those fine-tuned artifacts in the region associated with your tenant and do not replicate them cross-region for standard operation. Replication for disaster recovery may occur within the same legal region unless you opt into global HA. We can add a clause to the MSA that prevents cross-border replication for Orbis.

2) KV cache persistence:
- KV cache used for inference is in-memory by default and is not persisted to object storage. For some customers who request persistent caching (durable cache for performance), we persist encrypted cache blobs to customer-designated object storage or to our S3 buckets in the tenant region. We will flag any such persistence in the spreadsheet we deliver.

3) Deletion SLA (hosted):
- Live data: upon a verified deletion request, we purge request payloads from live systems within 72 hours.
- Backups & snapshots: standard process is to mark records for deletion immediately; complete removal from backups can take up to 30 days depending on backup cadence.
- We can contractually shorten those windows for Orbis in the MSA (e.g., 7 days for backups) for an enterprise commitment.

4) Cross-border copies:
- We do not intentionally move customer data outside the tenant-selected jurisdiction without explicit opt-in. Warm-pool/HA replication that would cross legal jurisdictions is opt-in only. I will include a signed attestation that confirms this for Orbis.

5) Evidence format & timeline:
- Deliverables we will provide by Fri 2027-07-09:
  * Signed attestation (single page PDF) confirming regional processing and non-replication unless opted-in.
  * Completed subprocessor mapping CSV (full row-level mapping for Orbis).
  * Data flow diagram rendered for Orbis requests (PNG/PDF).
  * Short procurement checklist (one page) enumerating the docs you can attach to procurement packet.

Attachments referenced earlier are drafts; we will produce the Orbis-specific exports and a signed attestation by Fri. Marissa will coordinate the formal paperwork and any required NDAs to share the more detailed telemetry exports.

If that timeline works, Marissa — can you pick a 30-minute slot tomorrow (Thu 7/8) to review the final artifacts with Orbis?

Thanks,
Dylan
Lead Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
(attachment: data_flow_diagram_orbis.png)
notes: Thread focuses on regional processing, subprocessor inventory, retention/deletion SLAs, and a commitment to deliver a signed attestation and Orbis-specific mapping by the requested deadline.
